description: The Dataset of Georeferenced Dams in South America (DDSA) lists 1,010 dams across South America with a combined reservoir volume of 1,017 cubic kilometres, compiled because regional and global inventories focused on the best-known basins such as the Amazon. Each dam has 24 attributes covering its name, characteristics, purposes and location, plus catchment hydrology: area, mean precipitation, temperature, potential evapotranspiration and runoff, population, area equipped for irrigation and, from version 1.0.1, aridity index, residence time and degree of regulation. Version 1.0.1 also adds a catchment shapefile and a table of future dams in South America. It was compiled at the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid from public and government records and published on Zenodo as CSV, shapefile and KMZ under CC BY 4.0, with a data paper in Earth System Science Data (2021); the authors ask users to notify them. Caveats: the inventory dates from 2020, completeness depends on national records, and small dams are missing. Simulation uses: dam and reservoir exposure to hazards, storage and regulation in capacity planning, and climate adaptation of reservoirs. Related records: GeoDAR (data-geodar-georeferenced-global-dams-reservoirs) and GRanD (data-grand-global-reservoir-and-dam-database).
